videos.title: Why There’s An ‘Extremely Fierce’ Battle For TSMC's Limited Chip Manufacturing Capacity
videos.description:
Unstoppable demand for AI is leading to a capacity crunch on factory lines at the world's leading chip manufacturer, Taiwan Semiconductor. And it could put a chokehold on AI's ability to scale. Analysts tell CNBC that Nvidia, Apple, Broadcom, AMD and others are locked in an “extremely fierce” competition to get their GPUs, CPUs and custom AI chips made at TSMC. Capacity can’t come online fast enough, despite TSMC’s rush to build new fabs in Taiwan, Japan and Arizona, where has expanded investment to $265 billion. The strain has made one man at TSMC “the most popular person on the planet,” as chip start-ups and big name CEOs visit Taiwan to ask him for wafer allocation. It’s also created a rich opportunity for Intel, as customers look to the long-struggling foundry arm of the U.S. chip manufacturer for a second source.

0:00 Introduction
2:06 ‘Most popular person on the planet’
6:54 Making room for smaller players
9:10 Can new U.S. fabs ease the crunch?

videos.title: Private Investment for Jobs | Quick Take
videos.description:
How can private capital mobilization unlock investment, support businesses, and create more and better jobs in emerging markets and developing economies?

Watch this quick take from the World Bank Group Annual Meetings flagship event: Unlocking Investment Opportunities in Emerging Markets to Create Jobs. 

World Bank Group President Ajay Banga joined investors, regulators, development finance leaders, and private sector partners to explore how to mobilize private investment at scale. The discussion focused on building investable project pipelines, using guarantees and other tools to share risk, expanding local-currency financing, strengthening domestic capital markets, and creating investment models that can be replicated across projects and markets.

Drawing on examples from infrastructure, energy, and small business financing, speakers explored how governments, development institutions, and the private sector can work together to connect capital with opportunity and support job creation.

videos.title: The Space Force Showed Us Its Weapons Used in Iran and Venezuela | WSJ Equipped
videos.description:
An array of U.S. Space Force electromagnetic warfare systems are playing a key role in protecting American troops and degrading enemy satellites around the world. 

The Journal was granted rare access to a Space Force base in Colorado to learn how those systems work, and to speak exclusively with Guardians who flew them overseas to support operations in both Venezuela and Iran.

Hours after Tech. Sgt. Joshua Lomax jammed satellites to create a protective bubble around U.S. forces capturing Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, he was given 72 hours to pack up his equipment and head to the Middle East, where the U.S. would soon launch its war against Iran.

videos.title: Movilizar inversiones para crear empleo en mercados emergentes | Reuniones Anuales de 2026
videos.description:
¿Qué se necesita para atraer más inversión privada a los mercados emergentes y convertirla en oportunidades de empleo?

Sigue «Movilizar inversiones para crear empleo en mercados emergentes» en vivo desde las Reuniones Anuales de 2026 en Bangkok. Ajay Banga, presidente del Grupo Banco Mundial, conversará con inversionistas, reguladores, aseguradoras y líderes de las finanzas para el desarrollo sobre cómo reducir los riesgos y abrir nuevas oportunidades de inversión.

La conversación abordará los mercados de capitales, el financiamiento en moneda local, las garantías, la titulización y las reformas de política pública. También examinará cómo movilizar capital privado puede apoyar a las empresas, el crecimiento económico y la creación de empleo.

Las Reuniones Anuales de 2026 reúnen a líderes de todo el mundo en Bangkok, del 12 al 18 de octubre, para debatir sobre empleo, inversión, crecimiento y soluciones prácticas para el desarrollo.

videos.title: Mobiliser l'investissement privé pour créer des emplois | Assemblées annuelles 2026
videos.description:
Comment attirer davantage d’investissements privés dans les marchés émergents et soutenir ainsi la création d’emplois ?

Suivez « Mobiliser l’investissement pour créer des emplois dans les marchés émergents » en direct des Assemblées annuelles 2026 à Bangkok. Ajay Banga, président du Groupe de la Banque mondiale, échangera avec des investisseurs, des autorités de régulation, des assureurs et des acteurs du financement du développement sur les moyens de réduire les risques et d’ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives d’investissement.

Le débat portera notamment sur les marchés de capitaux, le financement en monnaie locale, les garanties, la titrisation et les réformes. Il examinera comment la mobilisation de capitaux privés peut soutenir les entreprises, la croissance et l’emploi.

Les Assemblées annuelles 2026 réunissent des dirigeants du monde entier à Bangkok, du 12 au 18 octobre, autour de l’emploi, de l’investissement, de la croissance et du développement.

videos.title: How Cheap Mortgages Are Backfiring On Homeowners
videos.description:
Many Americans took advantage of historically low mortgage rates during the pandemic. But for homeowners who opted for adjustable-rate mortgages, those savings might not last. As mortgage rates continue to remain elevated, hundreds of thousands of borrowers are soon nearing the end of their introductory fixed-rate periods, putting them at risk of higher monthly payments. And with refinancing no longer offering the same relief it once did, some homeowners could find themselves facing a difficult financial decision.

videos.title: Why This Deep Red State Is a Battleground for the GOP’s Future | WSJ
videos.description:
Idaho, deeply Republican and mostly rural, is about the furthest you could get from a battleground state. So it is no surprise it is often overlooked in the national media during midterm elections.

But under the surface there is a groundswell of tensions between traditional Republicans, the MAGA loyalists and newer hardline-right politicians tussling for power and influence in Idaho. This Mountain West state has become a key bellwether for the fight over what a post-Trump Republican Party could become at the national level, as well as a test lab for some of the nation’s most controversial conservative legislation.

WSJ’s Robbie Gramer returns to his home state of Idaho to explore what the tensions between Idaho’s traditional Republicans and a newer, hard-line political right could mean for the Republican party’s national identity ahead of the midterms.

videos.title: Inside Man: How Chinese Spies Used Lies, Romance And Betrayal To Target The Federal Reserve
videos.description:
One week after a friendly summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, CNBC details an aggressive plot by China to infiltrate one of the United States’ most important institutions: the Federal Reserve. This explosive documentary delves into the incredible saga of a Chinese spy's effort to obtain secrets from the inner confines of the U.S.' top bank. It's a tale of sex, money, deceit and betrayal that put some of the country’s vital economic and financial secrets at risk. With exclusive access to new documents, audio, photos and text messages, CNBC's Senior Washington Correspondent Eamon Javers uncovers the story of former Fed economist John Rogers and a Chinese spy posing as an economics student who he befriended in 2013. “Inside Man” is a spy story at the heart of the competition for global economic dominance, posing the question of whether Rogers was a spy himself or an unwitting dupe.
